The assigned C trace reaches the monster-on-hero arm: a landed hit draws the existing magic-cancellation check, then the following pager step enters mon_poly/polyself and displays a freakish metamorphosis. Since mhitm_ad_poly uses mon_poly’s returned damage in its branches and mon_poly has no JavaScript implementation, the whole mhitm.c:mon_poly callee is a required same-task dependency.

source.branch: mhitm_adtyping dispatches AD_POLY for a landed monster attack. mhitm_ad_poly first checks magical negation or attacker mspec_used. For a monster attacking the hero (mdef == &gy.youmonst), it emits hitmsg and applies the Maybe_Half_Phys(damage) < current hero HP gate; if the attack is not negated it calls mon_poly, then sets M_ATTK_HIT and done. The recording confirms this successful monster-on-hero branch. The whole source function also includes hero-on-monster weaponless/nonlethal and monster-on-monster/nonlethal branches.
